rows: In 1970, in an evening assembly in Islington, Yogiji Maharaj prophesies that a traditional stone shikharbaddha mandir will be built in London
Yogiji Maharaj completes the historic inauguration of Islington Mandir, the first Swaminarayan Hindu mandir in the western hemisphere, on Sunday 14 June 1970

In 1982, Pramukh Swami Maharaj performed the image installation ceremony in the mandir on Meadow Garth, Neasden. Over time, it became apparent that a larger site would be needed in order to fulfil Yogiji Maharaj’s vision
In 1984, Pramukh Swami Maharaj visits the Ducker site in Harrow, a prime location for a traditional shikharbaddha mandir
Pramukh Swami Maharaj showers flower petals on the ground, blessing the land. However, opposition in the borough led to planning permission being withdrawn. The search for a suitable site continues…
Neasden High School was acquired and the ground-breaking ceremony for this site was performed on 24 June 1990
Upon returning from the ground-breaking ceremony at Neasden High School, Pramukh Swami Maharaj notices that the Arlington Bus and Coach Garage site is up for sale
Pramukh Swami Maharaj, along with senior devotees and trustees, visits the Arlington site

Pramukh Swami Maharaj discusses and observes initial drawings of the mandir to be built on the Arlington site with CM Patel, James Cornell, Nigel Lane, Akshaymunidas Swami, Madhusudan Patel, Amrish Patel and others
Pramukh Swami Maharaj on the new mandir site with the project team and trustees
The ground-breaking ceremony for the mandir takes place on 7 July 1991 in the presence of Pramukh Swami Maharaj and Mahant Swami
Pramukh Swami Maharaj performs the ground-breaking ceremony on the Arlington site

Pramukh Swami Maharaj visits the stone carving workshop set up in the free-trade zone in Kandla, Gujarat, India; he meticulously observes the carvings and ensures the work is completed on time and to the highest quality
Pramukh Swami Maharaj had instructed that the mandir be completed in three years, a seemingly impossible task
Senior swamis provide an update on the project to Pramukh Swami Maharaj during a site visit
A total of 26,300 pieces of stone were intricately carved for the main mandir construction. The carving primarily took place in Kandla.
CM Patel and Pramukh Swami Maharaj outside the old Meadow Garth hari mandir exchanging a jovial moment
The UK in the 1990s was experiencing a devastating recession, therefore funds were scarce. Subsequently, fundraising schemes – like the ‘Aluminium Can Collection’ scheme – were set up
Another such fundraising scheme – the ‘Care Patrika’ – being sanctified by Pramukh Swami Maharaj
Pramukh Swami Maharaj visits the construction site ensuring that the work is being done on time and to the highest quality
In order to complete the construction of the mandir on time, over 1,000 volunteers dedicated their efforts in helping out in whichever way they could
Devotees from across the UK would arrive early in the morning and work until late at night with a spirit of unity
Men and women of all ages were inspired to come together to help with whatever they could
Volunteers on site polishing one of the torans (decorative arches)
Workers and volunteers on site were fed three meals a day, freshly prepared by the large corps of female volunteers
Volunteers working tirelessly to keep the kitchen running efficiently
The mandir begins to take shape as the beautifully carved pillars are secured in place
Around 100 artisans are brought over from India to assist in the stone carving in the UK, speeding up the process of construction
As construction was well underway, the UK Satsang Mandal is shaken with the sudden passing of their chairman and close friend of Swamishri – CM Patel – in early 1994
With many questioning whether the mandir would be completed on time, Swamishri visits the construction site, inspiring and reinvigorating everyone
Pramukh Swami Maharaj proclaims that “patthar satsang karavshe” (the stones will spread the glory of satsang) in the UK
Despite suffering from a frozen shoulder and other physical health issues, Swamishri continues to drive the project forward by making regular visits to the construction site
Pramukh Swami Maharaj arrives in 1994 as devotees flock to pledge more funds for the successful completion of the mandir
Pramukh Swami Maharaj was heavily involved in the design of the mandir. Here, he visits one of the stone carving workshops in India to assess the models of the murtis
Pramukh Swami Maharaj strived for perfection. As the murtis arrive in the UK, he personally advises the craftsmen on what adjustments to make

Mahant Swami was also instrumental in the design of the murtis, advising fellow swamis and craftsmen to keep in line with the authentic description of Bhagwan Swaminarayan detailed by senior paramhansas
The mandir nears completion as the opening ceremony looms a mere few months away
Volunteers on site work throughout the night to get the mandir completed on time
The mandir nears completion as the opening ceremony looms a mere few months away
An aerial view of the mandir under construction in 1995
The main gate situated in front of the mandir under construction late at night in 1995
Pramukh Swami Maharaj arrives in the UK in July 1995 to oversee the final stages of the construction of the mandir
Pramukh Swami Maharaj regularly continues visiting the construction site, ensuring the timely and proper completion of the mandir
Pramukh Swami Maharaj on a site visit of the mandir and the haveli advising swamis and the project team on specific design elements
Pramukh Swami Maharaj advises the need for an exhibition on the lower floor of the mandir, to help explain Hinduism to the wider community in Britain

It was Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s wish to create a pillarless assembly hall. On his visits to the haveli complex, he would often point out design details and provide valuable guidance to the project team
The days of festivities leading up to the grand opening required marquees to be set up in Gibbons Recreational Ground where a number of events would be held
Pramukh Swami Maharaj visited each and every exhibit in the Bal Nagri (Children's Pavillion), participating in the interactive elements set up by volunteers

As per Hindu tradition, a grand procession took place allowing the murtis to bless the land and people of their new home. Beautiful floats were created on which the murtis could pass through the heart of the City of London
On 18 August 1995, the procession began at Hyde Park Corner and ended at Trafalgar Square, passing through Piccadilly Circus. Thousands gathered to be a part of this historic moment
To the surprise of every devotee present, Pramukh Swami Maharaj blessed everyone with his divine presence at Piccadilly Circus
A Vishwa Shanti Mahayagna was performed on 19 August 1995. At the time, it was the largest yagna to be performed outside of India
Pramukh Swami Maharaj performs the Vishwa Shanti Mahayagna, praying for peace and prosperity in the world
20 August 1995 – the day of the grand opening of the mandir. Pramukh Swami Maharaj stands before the murti of Bhagwan Swaminarayan as the image installation ceremony is under way

The haveli (cultural) complex was also opened by Swamishri on 20 August 1995. It incorporated a large, multi-purpose complex with a partitionable pillarless hall, offices, a gymnasium for children, and accommodation for the resident swamis

rows: On Tuesday 7 July 1970, Yogiji Maharaj departed from London for Mumbai via Paris, Zürich and Beirut. During the stopover in Paris, Swamishri requested Pramukh Swami and Mahant Swami to sanctify the land of Europe on his behalf
After that historic moment in 1970, Swayamprakashdas Swami (Doctor Swami) and swamis conducted the first vicharan in Europe in 1982
Facilities were scarce, therefore the group travelled around France in a small motorhome
The group sat in a park with the famous Eiffel Tower a mere stone’s throw away and conducted the first sabha in mainland Europe
Pramukh Swami Maharaj travelled to Europe in 1984, his maiden vicharan in mainland Europe as Guru. He is seen here standing with Shri Harikrishna Maharaj outside St Peter’s Basilica in Vatican City
Pramukh Swami Maharaj met Pope John Paul II, head of the Roman Catholic Church, at St Peter’s Basilica, where both exchanged respects and discussed interfaith dialogue and harmony
Pramukh Swami Maharaj visited many famous locations in Rome with Shri Harikrishna Maharaj, including the Colosseum
On 10 April 1984, Pramukh Swami Maharaj visited Hanbhai Kop’s home in the Netherlands, who gifted a thick red shawl to Swamishri as a memento of the occasion
Pramukh Swami Maharaj also visited Portugal in 1984
In 1986, Keshavjivandas Swami (Mahant Swami) and swamis embarked upon a research trip around the world for the upcoming Swaminarayan Akshardham in Gandhinagar
The group travelled across Europe by motorhome. Mahant Swami’s discipline towards his daily routine shone through, sitting outside the campervan on a camping site reading the Vachanamrut
The research tour in 1986 took Mahant Swami to various locations across mainland Europe
This vicharan proved helpful to Mahant Swami and the research team

In 1988, Pramukh Swami Maharaj embarked upon his second vicharan in mainland Europe. On 4 May, Swamishri flew over Paris in a helicopter, lifting Shri Harikrishna Maharaj and showering flower petals to bless the land below
Pramukh Swami Maharaj also took Shri Harikrishna Maharaj to the world-famous Eiffel Tower
Upon reaching the summit of the Eiffel Tower, Pramukh Swami Maharaj once again showered flower petals and blessed Paris by looking over the entire land through a telescope
Satsang in Paris was in its infancy in 1988. There were only a handful of devotees. Pramukh Swami Maharaj blessed the caravan home of a devotee
On 6 May 1988, Pramukh Swami Maharaj visited the Sanctuary of Fatima in Fatima, Portugal

The Chaplain of the Sanctuary, John Vilanova, brought the visitors book to Pramukh Swami Maharaj and requested he write something. Swamishri sat down on the stone steps and began to write his blessings as the Chaplain sat beside him
Pramukh Swami Maharaj then presided in a nearby park where a group of local children, out of excitement, surrounded Swamishri. He gifted them sanctified sweets as they departed
Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s vicharan of Europe also took him to Barcelona, Spain; in the spirit of Columbus’ Monument, Swamishri pointed in the direction of Akshardham
On 11 May 1988, Pramukh Swami Maharaj arrived in Switzerland; the harsh climate of Mount Säntis led to Swamishri being draped with a thick blanket
While on Mount Säntis. Pramukh Swami Maharaj gave everyone memories of a lifetime; in a divine, jovial mood, Swamishri threw snowballs at the swamis and devotees present
Upon leaving Mount Säntis, Pramukh Swami Maharaj sat down on a simple bench and prayed for the people of Switzerland and for the drought relief efforts taking place in India at the time
With a large group of swamis and devotees, Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s vicharan would often include travelling by coach
In May 1988, Pramukh Swami Maharaj visited Vienna, Austria, where the devotees had lovingly organised a horse carriage procession for Shri Harikrishna Maharaj and Swamishri through the city centre

On 13 May 1988, Pramukh Swami Maharaj visited Dusseldorf, Germany; after completing his walk in a large park, Swamishri sat on a shallow hill overlooking a lake with the swamis and devotees and began singing bhajans
On 19 May 1988, Pramukh Swami Maharaj arrived in Sweden, where the local devotees joyously greeted him at the airport with flower garlands and a musical welcome

While the construction of the first traditional Hindu temple outside of India was well underway in London, in 1994, Pramukh Swami Maharaj visited the Czech Republic upon the request of the renowned multimedia artist, Professor Jaroslav Frič
Professor Frič personally gave Pramukh Swami Maharaj a tour of Prague, asking him to bless the city and its key locations
During his visit to the churches, Pramukh Swami Maharaj also met with Bishop Skrdla, with whom he had a brief interfaith dialogue

Professor Frič brought Pramukh Swami Maharaj to one of the most revered sites in Prague, the Jan Hus Memorial, where he exclaimed that it was his duty to spread Swamishri’s glory in the Czech Republic
It was Professor Frič’s innermost wish that Pramukh Swami Maharaj travel along the Vltava River in Prague, so that Swamishri could further bless the city and all those gathered

In 1997, Pramukh Maharaj visited Paris to inaugurate the first BAPS mandir in mainland Europe. The traditional ‘nagar yatra’ of the murtis took place in the unconventional method of a boat ride at night
The following day, Pramukh Swami Maharaj conducted the Vedic inauguration ceremony
As the inauguration ceremony concluded, Pramukh Swami Maharaj sat down on the floor to sing the thal to the murtis
With satsang having developed in mainland Europe, Pramukh Swami Maharaj set off on what was to be his last traditional vicharan in mainland Europe by visiting France and Portugal in June 2000
During this vicharan, Pramukh Swami Maharaj inaugurated the first hari mandir in Lisbon, Portugal, in a small repurposed house
In September 2014, Mahant Swami and Bhaktipriyadas Swami (Kothari Swami) visited Lisbon for the inauguration of the new hari mandir, where they also presided over the nagar yatra in a horse carriage
On 28 September 2014, Mahant Swami and Kothari Swami performed the inauguration ceremony in the traditional Vedic manner
Mahant Swami and Kothari Swami also visited the Sanctuary of Fatima, where they reminisced on Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s visit there in 1988
Walking in their guru’s footsteps, Mahant Swami and Kothari Swami sat under the same tree Pramukh Swami Maharaj did in 1988 in Fatima

During this time, Bhadreshdas Swami had embarked upon a tour of Europe to discuss the newly written Swaminarayan Bhashyam with scholars across the continent. As the tour began in Lisbon, Mahant Swami blessed Bhadreshdas Swami in the motorhome in which he would travel

In 2014, despite his frail health and advanced age of 93, Pramukh Swami Maharaj travelled to Robbinsville, USA, to bless and perform pujan of the upcoming Swaminarayan Akshardham site. On his return to India, Swamishri’s flight stopped over in Paris, France
Pramukh Swami Maharaj was in a jovial mood having landed in Paris. Although he did not disembark from the aircraft, he blessed the land through his divine presence and gaze
Pramukh Swami Maharaj was in a jovial mood having landed in Paris. Although he did not disembark from the aircraft, he blessed the land through his divine presence and gaze

In October 2017, Mahant Swami Maharaj set off on his maiden vicharan of mainland Europe as Guru. One morning in France, Swamishri unexpectedly stepped out onto the balcony of the chateau to bless the gathered devotees

On 16 October 2017, the Mayor of Bussy-Saint-Georges, Yann Dubosc, met with Mahant Swami Maharaj. In the evening sabha, the Mayor expressed his wish to bestow upon Swamishri the 'Medal of Honour' and invited him to visit the Parisian suburb of Bussy-Saint-Georges

As the days of Diwali were approaching, on 17 October 2017, Mahant Swami Maharaj celebrated Diwali and Annakut in Paris. Sitting down on the floor, Swamishri devoutly sang the thal. The following day, Swamishri returned to the UK, marking the end of his vicharan in mainland Europe

/Photos/2025/Ancient-India-living-tradit.t: Neasden Temple Named Community Partner in British Museum Exhibition on Ancient Indian Sacred Art, London, UK
rows: A special community event to launch the exhibition was hosted in the British Museum’s Queen Elizabeth II Great Court

Dr Nicholas Cullinan OBE, Director of the British Museum, welcomed the guests and introduced the exhibition as one of the first in the world to look at the early devotional art of India from a multi-faith, contemporary and global perspective
The Rt Hon George Osborne CH, Chair of the British Museum’s Board of Directors, also lauded the exhibition’s role in raising awareness about the rich heritage of India’s sacred art
Mr Osborne added that the exhibition had been developed in collaboration with an advisory community panel of practising Hindus, Buddhists and Jains
BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, London, has been acknowledged by the curators as a community partner for the exhibition
As a part of the inauguration of the exhibition, a volunteer from Neasden Temple chanted Hindu prayers from the Upanishads and Satsang Diksha
He conveyed the best wishes of everyone at Neasden Temple for the growing awareness of Hindu art and spirituality
A leading member of the British Jain community offered prayers from Jain texts
Monks of the Buddhist tradition also offered traditional prayers for the exhibition
A sitar- and tabla-player further embellished the atmosphere with classical Indian music
The exhibition aims to highlight the provenance of each artefact on show, examining their stories from creation to acquisition
The Mandir also features in the exhibition’s accompanying publication as an example of India’s ancient art living on today in active places of worship
Kayte McSweeney, Community Partnerships Manager at the British Museum, showed volunteers from Neasden Temple some of the 180 objects on display in the exhibition

At another inauguration event, Kajal Meghani, Project Curator for the exhibition, again appreciated the contributions of Neasden Temple in helping raise awareness about Hindu art and architecture, citing their many visits and consultation sessions

rows: The United Nations Office at Vienna (UNOV) is one of four secretariats of the UN, after Geneva, Nairobi, and the headquarters in New York

Volunteers provided the event passes to all registrants

The venue of the Diwali celebration was Conference Room 1
Each delegate received a decorative diya (traditional lamp), printed programme, and an information leaflet about BAPS Swaminarayan Hindu Mandir, Paris
Ambrish Limbachia, a senior BAPS volunteer from the UK, welcomed the delegates and introduced the theme of ‘Light, Peace, and Partnership’
More than 170 delegates joined the cultural and commemorative Diwali celebration
The proceedings began with Vedic prayers for universal peace and well-being
The soulful singing by swamis was accompanied by traditional Indian instruments

Vikram Jeet Duggal, Counsellor at the Permanent Mission of India to the UN, and Rushin Thacker, BAPS Representative at the UN Office in Vienna, participated in the ceremonial lighting of the decorative lamps
The event marked 25 years since the landmark address of HH Pramukh Swami Maharaj at the Millennium World Peace Summit at the UN headquarters in New York
Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s call for multi-level dialogue – amongst religious leaders, with their respective followers, and with oneself – felt just as relevant for peace 25 years on
Dr Markand Patel expanded upon 30 years of BAPS’s partnership with the United Nations
Dr Patel is a leading volunteer for BAPS healthcare services across the UK
Dr Patel systematically explained the work of BAPS in supporting the UN’s various ‘Sustainable Development Goals’ to help end poverty, protect the planet, and ensure peace and prosperity for all
Vikram Jeet Duggal, Counsellor at the Permanent Mission of India, delivered the keynote address, commending the shared ethos of Diwali, BAPS and the UN
Mr Duggal praised the values-based leadership of Mahant Swami Maharaj in guiding BAPS’s services for humanity, calling him a “true Ambassador of Love, Peace, and Harmony in our world today”
Ms Peri Lynne Johnson, Assistant Director General and Legal Adviser of the UN’s International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA), shared some remarks as the guest of honour
Ms Johnson appreciated BAPS’s work in the Ukraine humanitarian crisis and also its activities in the United States, saying, “Hearing the work of BAPS feels like home again.”
Earlier, BAPS volunteers met with Ms Johnson and the Permanent Mission of India to further discuss shared values and goals
International diplomats sat alongside BAPS volunteers
Diplomats and dignitaries from various countries, UN agencies, and community organisations joined the celebration
Brahmaviharidas Swami, Head of the BAPS Hindu Mandir in Abu Dhabi, shared an inspiring video message on cultivating ‘Peace through Partnership’
The delegates were introduced to BAPS’s growing role in promoting interfaith and multicultural understanding in Europe through the forthcoming BAPS Swaminarayan Hindu Mandir in Paris
In a recorded message, Mr Yann Dubosc, Mayor of Bussy-Saint-Georges in Paris, shared: “BAPS’s work across countless local communities shows that spirituality and service can go hand in hand.”

Guest of Honour Mr Yuko Yasunaga, Deputy Director General and Managing Director of the UN’s Industrial Development Organization (UNIDO), underlined the importance of partnership between public institutions and civil society
Mr Yasunaga congratulated BAPS on its 25 years of General Consultative Status with ECOSOC, and reiterated the need to “work together… as good neighbours, hand in hand.”
International diplomats sat alongside BAPS representatives from around the world

BAPS representatives from Australia, Austria, France, Germany, the Netherlands, New Zealand, Portugal, Sweden, and the United Kingdom were also among the delegates, reflecting the fellowship’s global reach and its continuing partnership with the UN family

Rena Amin, a senior volunteer for BAPS UK & Europe, concluded the proceedings by thanking the delegates and sharing a call for further partnership “so that we may continue to grow together in serving humanity”

His Eminence Cardinal George Jacob Koovakad, the head of the Catholic Church's Dicastery for Interreligious Dialogue, recognised the BAPS swamis and greeted them before the inaugural session of the conference
The Rector Magnificus of the Angelicum, Fr. Thomas Joseph White, O.P., was also pleased to see Paramtattvadas Swami again and welcomed him to the conference

In his keynote address, Cardinal Koovakad reiterated the value and need for genuine dialogue, fraternity and collaboration amongst faith communities in the world today
Delegates included religious leaders, scholars, academics, and representatives of dharmic faith communities from across Europe
